questions.question: Explain two Muslim beliefs about the nature of Allah.

points.text: 1) Allah is transcendent — he is above and beyond the created universe and beyond full human understanding. Surah 42:11 states "There is nothing like Him," meaning Allah cannot be compared to anything in creation. 2) Allah is immanent — he is close to his creation and present everywhere. questions.question: "Tawhid is the most important Muslim belief." Evaluate this statement.

points.text: Tawhid is indeed the foundation of Islam — it is the first part of the Shahadah and the message of all prophets. Without tawhid, no other belief makes sense. However, some might argue that other beliefs are equally important for daily life: the Five Pillars give structure to Muslim practice, and belief in akhirah motivates moral behaviour.
